extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in mathematical physics / symplectic geometry (readers of a PhD dissertation on BRST cohomology)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formatting/organizational conventions for a PhD dissertation in mathematical physics (BRST cohomology, symplectic geometry, homological algebra), plus methodological advice for computing cohomology (spectral sequences, double complexes, resolutions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissertation structure and chapter/section/appendix numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapters are numbered in upper case roman numerals, sections in arabic numerals, and appendices in upper case latin letters. A reference to a section or an appendix within the same chapter shall only contain its number; whereas a reference to a section or appendix on a different chapter shall also contain the chapter number. Subsections are not numbered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the indicated numbering scheme consistently across the dissertation so cross-references are unambiguous (e.g., refer to Section II.2 when referencing Section 2 of Chapter II from outside that chapter, but just 'Section 2' within Chapter II).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation and 'mathematica' (definitions/theorems/etc.) numbering convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Equations and mathematica (i.e., definitions, theorems, ...) are numbered sequentially within a section or appendix and also contain the number of the chapter (e.g., (III.2.1) refers to the first numbered equation of the second section of the third chapter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number items with the composite chapter.section.item format to make their location immediately clear; follow sequential numbering per section/appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of Section 0 equations (TeX glitch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equations which appear to be in Section 0 appear at the beginning of the relevant chapter before the start of the first section (a minor TeX nichal glitch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of this TeX peculiarity when locating/labeling equations that seem to belong to Section 0; they should be treated as part of the chapter preamble and numbered consistently with the chapter/section scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Halmos notation to mark end-of-proof
rubrics_metrics.description: We use Halmos’ notation to signify the end of a proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminate proofs with the standard Halmos tombstone (end-of-proof symbol) to make proof endings explicit and consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box particularly interesting equations for emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Particularly interesting equations have been boxed for emphasis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight especially important or central displayed equations by boxing them so readers can quickly locate key formulae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes are numbered sequentially throughout the dissertation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a single continuous sequence of footnote numbers across the whole dissertation rather than resetting per chapter/section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boldfaced words appear in index
rubrics_metrics.description: Boldfaced words (except for that one) appear in the index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark terms to be indexed by boldfacing them in the text so the index is automatically aligned with emphasized terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an index of jargon at the end
rubrics_metrics.description: An index of jargon has been provided at the end of the dissertation for the convenience of the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and define specialized terminology in a single index to help readers unfamiliar with field-specific vocabulary; ensure boldfaced/in-text cues match index entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typesetting environment and macros
rubrics_metrics.description: This dissertation has been typeset entirely in TeX6 — the computer typesetting environment created by Donald Knuth — using a mix of macros defined by D. Knuth, V. Kaplunowsky, and the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State and use a consistent typesetting system and macro package (here Straight TeX / TeX6 and specified macros) so output is reproducible and formatting conventions (numbering, boxed equations, etc.) behave predictably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage readers to skim preliminaries for notation
rubrics_metrics.description: The reader is strongly urged to at least skim this chapter for notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place essential notation and convention material early (e.g., a preliminaries chapter) and remind readers to consult it to reduce confusion later in the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectral sequences as a method to approximate/cohomology (practical prescription)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spectral sequences can be thought of as perturbation theory for cohomology: approximate the cohomology H of a complex by computing the early (first and/or second) terms (E1, E2) of a spectral sequence; if differentials vanish at an early stage the sequence degenerates and yields H directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When confronted with a complex whose cohomology you must compute, find a filtered or double-complex decomposition giving a spectral sequence converging to the target cohomology; compute E1/E2 (which are often easy) and check whether higher differentials vanish to conclude H or obtain vanishing theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical spectral-sequence procedure for double complexes
rubrics_metrics.description: For a double complex (K, D', D'') form the total complex TotK with D = D' + D''. Use the two canonical filtrations (horizontal and vertical) to produce two spectral sequences: the E1 term of one is the D' cohomology followed by D'' cohomology (''Hq('Hp(K))) and vice versa; these spectral sequences converge (under finiteness/boundedness hypotheses) to the graded pieces of the total cohomology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice, compute the D' (horizontal) cohomology rowwise to obtain 'Hp(K, q), then compute the D'' cohomology of that to get successive approximations to the total cohomology. Use boundedness to ensure convergence; choose the filtration whose early terms are easiest to compute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use projective (or acyclic-in-positive-degree) resolutions to simplify cohomology computations
rubrics_metrics.description: A special kind of resolution is one in which Cn = 0 for all n > 0 (a projective resolution); such resolutions give exact augmented complexes whose cohomology is concentrated in degree 0, providing computational simplifications and trace/Euler-characteristic formulas (e.g., Tr_H f* = sum_n (-1)^n Tr_{C^n} f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, replace an object by a resolution with trivial higher cohomology so that computations reduce to finite-dimensional linear algebra on the resolution; use the resulting Euler characteristic and trace identities to derive invariants such as Euler characteristics and to aid in proofs (e.g., no-ghost theorems).
